CHORALE estimates a shared biological state across omics modalities that were measured on different
individuals, and expresses that state in named biological terms.

## The problem

Most public omics data were not deposited as one study. A transcriptome comes from one set of
individuals, a proteome from another, a metabolome from a third. No individual appears twice, so there
is no row that both matrices describe. Standard integration needs one of three things: the same
individuals in both modalities, the same features in both, or a translation learned from paired
examples. A collection assembled from separate deposits offers none of them.

## What connects the modalities

The connecting object is a fixed vocabulary of named biological concepts. A concept is a set of
features that belong together for a stated biological reason, such as a curated pathway or a cell
type signature. Every modality is scored on the same concepts: for each sample, how high the
features carrying that concept sit relative to the rest of the cohort. A concept is the same
concept in every modality, because its name and its membership were fixed before any data were
looked at.

That is what removes the missing pairing from the problem. Two modalities need not share an
individual, and need not share a feature, in order to be compared on how far a named piece of
biology moves with the disease in each of them.

## What the design is for

The design supplies the evidence. Within each modality, the concept score is regressed on the
phenotype and on whatever covariates the modality records, giving one adjusted case-control effect
per concept per modality. A concept is supported when those effects agree in direction and are
large relative to their standard errors in the modalities that express it.

The direction of inference follows from the choice of connecting object. Where the design connects
modalities, the burden falls on it to identify one correspondence among several hundred candidate
pairings from two or three design terms, which independently deposited studies cannot carry.
Where concepts connect modalities, the design answers a different and far easier question: whether a
named concept separates cases from controls, one modality at a time, over a few hundred
prespecified hypotheses under error control.

## What lies outside the vocabulary

A fixed vocabulary bounds what the concept channel can express. Biology absent from it would
otherwise disappear silently, so the concept scores are removed from each assay and what remains is
decomposed into free dimensions. A free dimension that moves with the phenotype is coordinated
variation the vocabulary has no name for, and it is reported as such rather than forced into a
concept that does not describe it.

## What a supported concept establishes

A supported concept is a coordinated case-control shift in a named piece of biology, seen in more
than one measurement layer, at a stated error rate. Ordering cause and consequence requires timing,
mediation or perturbation, none of which a cross-sectional collection carries.

The vocabulary is where interpretation is fixed, so its choice is part of the analysis rather than a
presentational step after it. A concept that no modality has enough features for cannot be tested,
and coverage is reported per concept for that reason.

## A useful negative result

A collection in which no concept is supported still says something. The coverage report states how
many concepts each modality could be scored on at all. The free dimensions state whether coordinated
variation exists outside the vocabulary. Together these separate two situations that a bare absence
of results confuses: a collection carrying no shared signal, and a collection whose shared signal
the chosen vocabulary cannot name.
